summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to separate ML systems. Capabilities range from in-database model training (BigQuery ML, Redshift ML, Aurora ML) to native vector search for RAG and semantic search (Databricks, MongoDB Atlas) and fully managed LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex). Industry data suggests that by 2026 roughly 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search, with PostgreSQL and other general-purpose platforms gaining ground over purpose-built vector databases like Pinecone and Milvus.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI — managed LLM and ML functions
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless SQL and Python functions for LLM tasks (summarize, translate, sentiment, complete, extract), access to hosted foundation models (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Claude via Cortex), Cortex Search for retrieval, and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. It also extends to Snowflake Postgres, letting developers call Cortex AI functions against Postgres-managed data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector support via the VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), plus Cortex Search as a managed hybrid retrieval service.
databases.llm_integration: First-party hosted LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Claude, Snowflake Arctic) exposed through Cortex functions; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions are billed per token/credits consumed, separate from warehouse compute.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models using standard SQL (regression, classification, clustering, time series, matrix factorization) and invoke remote Vertex AI / Gemini models for generative tasks, embeddings, and inference directly in queries via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native vector search supported through the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings stored in BigQuery.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models; supports both Google-hosted foundation models and custom Vertex endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (bytes processed) or capacity-based slots for BigQuery; remote model inference incurs separate Vertex AI charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension and pgai for embeddings and LLM workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) brings embedding generation and LLM calls into SQL. This makes Postgres a popular general-purpose foundation for RAG and semantic search without a dedicated vector database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided by the third-party pgvector extension (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes). Marked false because it requires an extension rather than being built into vanilla Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai and related extensions that call external providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) from SQL; no native hosted LLM.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs depend on hosting (self-managed or managed providers like RDS, Cloud SQL, Timescale) plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL integration with SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions and generative AI to applications using SQL functions that call Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend, enabling inference and text generation directly from Aurora MySQL/PostgreSQL queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora itself has no native vector engine; vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is achieved via the pgvector extension, so it is not built-in native vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker endpoints via SQL functions for generative and predictive tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/IO pricing; ML inference costs are billed separately by SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training via SageMaker)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using standard SQL CREATE MODEL statements, with Amazon SageMaker Autopilot handling training behind the scenes. It also supports bring-your-own-model and generative AI via integration with Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector index/search engine in Redshift; vector similarity must be handled externally or approximated manually, so native vector search is not supported.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker for generative and predictive inference invoked from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute (RPU/node) pricing; model training and inference consume SageMaker resources billed separately.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search on the Lakehouse
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides tooling to build, fine-tune, serve, and govern ML and GenAI models, including foundation model serving, agent frameworks, and MLflow lifecycle management. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated with Unity Catalog and Delta tables for RAG.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in managed Vector Search service that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables with governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving hosts foundation models and custom models; integrates with external LLM providers and supports fine-tuning and agent workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based DBU pricing; Vector Search and Model Serving billed as separate serverless compute units.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic search and RAG
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational documents and running approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, combining vector, full-text, and metadata filtering in a single query for RAG and semantic applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search powered by HNSW indexing within Atlas; embeddings and operational data live together in the same documents with no separate vector store required.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with external LLM and embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Vertex, Bedrock) and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex; no first-party hosted LLM.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas cluster pricing (dedicated tiers); vector search uses cluster or dedicated Search Node compute billed as part of Atlas.
